标题: 浓烟半分钟上蹿百米 ！ 高层建筑失火为何难扑灭 ？
正文: 11月26日，香港大埔多栋住宅楼发生重大火灾事故，致数十人遇难。至次日晚，灭火救援工作仍在继续。为何高层建筑起火难以扑灭？如何科学自救？ 高楼起火为何蔓延快，扑救难？ 据香港消防处披露，香港大埔宏福苑于26日14时51分发生火警，15时34分火警升为四级，并于18时22分升为五级——仅次于最高等级“灾难级”。至27日晚，消防处的灭火救援工作仍然持续进行。 据悉，该楼群落成于1983年，共有8座楼宇，每座31层。火灾蔓延至7座大厦，仅剩一座大厦未被波及。 11月26日拍摄的火灾救援现场。新华社记者 陈铎 摄 为何火势发展如此迅猛？与普通建筑相比，高层建筑“立体燃烧”的复杂性更为突出。 首先，“烟囱效应”会使火势迅速蔓延。 “烟囱效应”是指户内空气沿着垂直坡度的空间向上升或下降，造成空气加强对流的现象。在高层建筑内部，楼梯间、管道井等各种竖向管井构造如同烟囱。火灾发生时，易形成气流对流，使得烟气和火焰迅速蔓延。 建筑高度越高，烟囱效应越明显。在火灾发展阶段，高层建筑中的烟火垂直蔓延速度平均为每秒3～4米，在超高层建筑（100米以上）中甚至可以达到每秒8米。也就是说，浓烟从一座30层、高约100米的建筑一楼蔓延至顶楼仅需30秒。 其次，高处风力大，使火势更难以控制。 建筑高度大于27m的住宅，大于24m的非单层厂房仓库和其他民用建筑，都属于高层建筑。据测定，高层建筑30米处风速8.7米/秒，60米处风速12.3米/秒，90米处风速可达到15米/秒。楼层越高，风速越大，火灾发生后往往会出现风助火势、火借风威，越烧越旺的态势。 此外，易燃可燃外保温材料也是重要“帮凶”。 我国从2005年开始推行建筑节能政策，主要措施之一就是在外墙增加保温层，由于以前对外墙保温材料危险性认识不足，对材料的燃烧性能并无明确规定，当时多采用聚苯乙烯泡沫板或聚氨酯硬质泡沫等易燃可燃材料，这些材料极易引燃且蔓延迅速，燃烧后产生大量有毒烟气，火灾危险性很大。 此次香港大埔火灾事故中，香港警方调查发现，建筑物外墙有保护网、防水帆布、塑料布，疑未符合防火标准，另有一座未波及的大厦每层电梯大堂窗外都有发泡胶包封，易燃且可能加速火势蔓延，不排除发泡胶是火势迅速蔓延的原因。 遭遇火情，“跑”还是“等”？ 高层建筑发生火灾时，是立即逃生，还是等待救援？ 发生火灾时，最好能判断火源点，再判断先灭火还是逃生。在火源确定且火势可控状态时，切忌惊慌失措，应利用周围的灭火器、消火栓等消防设施器材协助扑救初起火灾。 如无法扑灭，需要根据火势和烟雾情况来应对，做到“小火快跑、浓烟关门”。 🔸 “小火快跑”： 开门前先触摸门把手，若温度不高，且门缝无烟气渗入，再开门。如果火势没有挡住逃生路线，疏散楼梯间无明显烟气，应尽快逃生。 逃生时用浸湿的毛巾或衣物捂好口鼻，减少烟气对呼吸道的侵害；弯腰低姿态前行，避开上方浓烟；不要乘坐电梯，穿越常闭式防火门时应随手关门。 🔸 “浓烟关门”： 如果入户门把手发热，门底缝隙有烟气渗入，说明大火或浓烟已封锁房门出口，千万别贸然打开房门；如果门把手不热，开门发现走廊里没有烟，但楼梯间里有烟，也应立即退回室内。这种情况下，不要盲目开门逃生，因为几口有毒的浓烟就会让人昏厥，进而窒息身亡。 应立即关上房门，用湿毛巾封堵门缝，减少烟气进入，拨打119告知自己被困房间的位置，等待救援。同时不断用水淋湿入户门，防止外部高温烘烤，火势蔓延。在靠近窗口的位置通过打手电筒、挥舞衣物等方式发出求救信号。 逃生时，向上跑还是向下跑？ 遭遇高层建筑起火，符合“小火快跑”的撤离条件时，应该向上跑还是向下跑呢？ 这需要从起火楼层与自己的相对位置、具体火情来判断： 🔸火势可控且逃生通道畅通时，优先往下跑。 火灾发生在上方楼层，从容向下撤离，记得关闭窗户，防止火星进入；火灾来自同一楼层或下方，且疏散楼梯间无明显烟气，应尽快向下跑。 在疏散逃生时，要熟悉了解所居住场所的疏散通道和安全出口位置情况，一般高层建筑都有至少两部以上的楼梯可供疏散，着火时切勿使用电梯。 🔸 遇特殊情况迫不得已时，再考虑往上跑。 专家一般不建议向上跑，一是很难跑过烟气蔓延；二是逃离过程中被烟熏，有中毒危险，不如在家用湿毛巾把门缝堵实。 但遭遇极端情况，比如火灾发生在下方楼层，但向下逃生通道被封堵，无法安全撤离，且所在房间已无法停留、必须转移时，可以考虑向上跑，尽量跑到便于消防登高车触及的窗口，选择相对安全的楼层暂时躲避，或通过天台进入相邻单元逃生。 此次香港大埔火灾事故中，消防员于27日11时在一座大厦的31楼成功救出一名男性长者，为其戴上呼吸器后带至天台，成功由天台救到地面并将其送院进行救治。 此外，对于超高层建筑，在逃生受阻情况下，人员可就近疏散到避难层——相关规定要求，建筑高度大于100米的住宅或公共建筑必须设置消防

标题: 汕头自建房火灾始末|楼房|陈辉|铺面|五金店|汕头市
正文: 事发五金店。澎湃新闻记者 陈灿杰 图 这是一栋典型的潮汕地区“三合一”自建房，一楼开五金店，二楼作仓储，三楼住着奶奶和父母，四楼住着兄弟三家人。 几十年间，临街铺面从三间扩容成五间，看着蒸蒸日上。 直到一场大火毁了所有。三代人经营的五金店没了，四代同堂的家族中，12人丧生。 12月9日晚，位于广东汕头潮南区峡山街道的这栋四层自建房发生重大火灾，潮南区消防救援大队发布警情通报称，过火面积约150平方米。 火灾发生后，澎湃记者实地走访发现，事发地所在的峡山街道丹凤路上，多为类似的“三合一”式建筑，即经营、仓库、住宿混合，多处一楼店铺闭门停业。 仍在营业的数家商铺经营者均提到，今年以来已接受多次消防检查，沿街店铺需配有喷淋、烟感、灭火器等消防设施，否则停电停水。然而，一名知情人士称，事发五金店此前已办理消防合格证，但更多可能是应付日常检查，“除了喷淋没水，烟感也不正常”。 12月10日上午，广东省政府召开全省安全生产和消防工作视频会议，要求深刻汲取汕头“12·9”自建房重大火灾教训，对立即开展重大火灾风险隐患排查整治行动进行动员部署。近日，澎湃新闻在当地看到，当地已有建筑在安装防火门，以将楼下经营场所与楼上区隔。 中冶建筑研究总院（深圳）有限公司正高级工程师闵红光博士向澎湃新闻表示，“三合一”自建房是火灾高风险区，因可燃物多，没有严格的防火分隔，缺乏必要的消防设施设备，“一旦起火，极易导致群死群伤”。他建议，应建立房屋安全档案并信息化管理，建立跨部门综合监管体系，对自建房进行每年不少于一次的定期检查。 “主要就是那个烟在冲上去” 邻居陈辉说，发生火灾的五金店一般开到晚上近11点，常能看到店主和儿子在店里喝茶，事发当天，他们恰好关门较早。 这家店名为裕丰五金电器店，吴先生是店主的大儿子，起火时不在家。当晚9点22分，他接到妻子电话，得知家中失火，随后紧忙报警并驱车回家。 他赶到店里时，是9点28分，妻子两臂拽着两个小孩从店后门跑出，十岁的大女儿则已经打开正门逃生，“头发还被火烧焦了”，大女儿“应该是被黑烟熏到眼睛，看不见，没有方向感，就往前面冲”。吴先生说自己两次尝试进入正门，都被浓烟呛了出来。他的另外三个孩子和其他亲人还在着火的房子里。 当时，住在五金店对门的林斌和街坊一起，从紧邻厂房的消防栓接消防水带灭火，但很快发现是杯水车薪，“主要就是那个烟在冲上去”。现场视频显示，透过该店临街一侧关着的木头正门，能看到店内有剧烈火光，浓烟滚滚。伴随店内响彻街头的燃爆声，火势瞬间冲出门缝。 据相关道路监控信息，9点24分前后，距五金店约4.6公里的峡山消防救援站出动了两辆消防车；9点32分，距五金店约2.2公里的峡山管区消防义务队出动了一辆消防车。另据多名参与救火的街坊回忆，报警后共有6辆消防车陆续抵达，除上述两支消防队外，还有距五金店约9公里的司马浦消防救援站派车支援。 当时，吴先生未逃出来的三个孩子躲在房子后侧三楼的防盗窗处，等待救援。 在五金店后门协助救火的邻居陈辉回忆说，当时楼下聚着近二十个街坊，还有人关心三个孩子的安危，用手电筒照着。消防员随后到场升起云梯，用工具剪掉窗外的防盗网将小孩救下。陈辉记不清救下三个孩子花了多长时间，“那个时候连颤抖和害怕的时间都没有，只是帮忙了”。 澎湃新闻记者在现场向陈辉核实，房子三楼处有破拆痕迹的防盗网，即3个小孩逃生处。房子其余各层窗户均有防盗网，部分设置了逃生口，但未打开。尚不清楚逃生口是否上锁，以及遇难者生前是否曾尝试打开。 吴先生回忆说，3个小孩获救后，他以为其他人都跑向了天台。楼内有两个楼梯，分别在楼中间（连接正门）与楼的一侧，均可直通天台，“没有隔断的，只需要一分钟，甚至三十秒都能上去”。而上到天台后有三扇门，“两个没锁，可以直接打开”。 最终，吴先生等来了最为痛心的结果。他得知，除他与妻儿一家八口幸存，其余12位亲人躲在厕所或房间内，全部遇难，包括他的奶奶、父母和两个弟弟及其家人。事后他重返楼内，发现火几乎没烧到楼上，“人是被烟呛死的”。他说，见到遗体时，有遇难亲人的眼睛“还睁开（着）”，他试着把他们的眼睛合上。 从起火到明火被扑灭，过去了43分钟。据汕头市潮南区消防大队发布的警情通报，火灾发生的具体时间是12月9日21时20分，接报后，消防部门迅速调派力量赶赴救援，22时03分，现场明火被扑灭。 事发后，澎湃新闻拍客曾进入火灾现场，发现楼上屋内家具完整，几株植物仍然存活，但阳台和室内烟熏痕迹明显。 高层自建房火灾，浓烟可能是导致死亡的重要原因之一。中国消防科普委员会专家委员刘祖河接受中国新闻周刊采访时说，一旦楼下起火，高温、浓烟和有毒气体沿楼梯急速上蹿，迅速吞噬逃生通道，留给楼上居民的反应时间和逃生空间都极为有限。 据微信公号“广东消防”文章，今年6月14日凌晨，汕头一四层自建房突发大火

正文: ATLANTIC CITY, N.J. (WPVI) -- A fire early Wednesday forced several hundred residents from the Brighton Towers condominiums in Atlantic City, New Jersey, leaving nine units unlivable and sending one police officer to the hospital with minor injuries, according to building management and city officials. The fire appeared to have started in a bedroom on the building's eighth floor. While most residents were allowed back inside after crews brought the incident under control, those living in several corner units remained displaced. The evacuation began around 5 a.m., when residents were jolted awake by pounding on their doors. "Grab your coats and just leave. Or just grab whatever and just leave," resident Deep Halvawala said. "We didn't even have a minute to do anything." Another resident, Perry Lippowitsch, said false alarms were common in the building - but this time the danger was real. "It was pretty scary. Somebody banging on your door. Fire alarms go off a lot. It's usually a false alarm. This time it wasn't," he said. Lippowitsch said he rushed to reach his elderly mother in her unit. "Grabbed the shirt on my back. Went to get out of there. I got my 93-year-old mom, made sure she got out. At least we're all safe," he said. Fire officials said several residents with mobility challenges required assistance evacuating. "We took them out on balconies, covered them in blankets. We kept a firefighter with them," Acting Chief Paul Hess said. "We said we're going back. We had to be able to get them down an evacuation stairwell." Five residents were evaluated on scene and did not need medical treatment, according to city officials. Atlantic City Fire Chief Scott Evans said crews are well acquainted with the property. The high-rise, built in 1966, was the site of a deadly fire in 1969 that killed four people. Evans said the department continues to respond to frequent calls at the building. 标题: E - bike battery caused blaze that sent 2 people to hospital : Edmonton firefigh
正文: A blaze that broke out this week at an Edmonton highrise forcing dozens from their homes was caused by a lithium ion battery from an electric bike, officials said as they warned of an increase in these kinds of fires. Assistant Deputy Chief Justin Lallemand of Edmonton Fire Rescue Services said the apartment fire happened Wednesday evening from an electric bike stored on a sixth-floor balcony. Lallemand said two people were sent to hospital and 80 people were evacuated from the building. He added that 20 people have not been able to return to their units. “Over the last few years, as lithium ion batteries become more of a common part of our day, we have seen an increase in fires with these batteries as the cause,” Lallemand said at a news conference Friday. He said firefighters investigated eight fires linked to lithium-ion batteries last year. Get breaking National news “While that number appears small, these fires are extremely dangerous to people and property, and can cause challenges for our crews when they arrive to put them out.” He said it is also illegal to dispose of such batteries in the garbage, noting that there have been 24 battery-related fires over the past two years in the city’s waste management facilities. Lallemand said people should dispose of lithium ion batteries at the city’s eco stations or retailers with the appropriate recycling programs. He also advised people to use the correct batteries and their specific chargers provided or recommended by the manufacturer. “Do not charge devices any longer than necessary and ensure that you are not charging them near any exits you would use to evacuate your home,” he said. “Do not alter or modify the batteries they are using to power micro-mobility devices, power tools, or other battery-operated devices around your home.” Video on social media of the apartment blaze on Wednesday shows fire engulfing the balcony, with flames and smoke shooting out. 标题: People climbed down using saree : Horror moments from blaze in Delhi apartment
正文: NEW DELHI: A fire broke out in a five-storey residential building in southeast Delhi’s Govindpuri in the early hours of Friday. The incident occurred around 2. 30am in Tughlakabad Extension, killing three people and leaving two others critically injured. As thick smoke and flames engulfed the structure, residents made frantic attempts to escape. Some climbed out of windows using sarees, while others shouted for help from the rooftop, police said. Neighbours recalled scenes of panic and desperation. Rajan, a resident of the area, said smoke was first noticed around 2 am and soon filled the narrow lane where the building stands, news agency PTI reported. “We tried dousing the fire, but two-wheelers parked inside the building were already in flames. Since there were flammable materials, it helped the fire spread through the whole building,” he said further. With smoke spreading rapidly inside the building, trapped residents had little choice but to seek alternative escape routes, eyewitnesses said. “People saved their lives by using sarees to climb out of windows. Many people managed to get out through the back door of the building,” Rajan said. Neelu Devi, a local resident, said, “The smoke had entered our building as well.  As soon as we realised it, we ran out of our houses.” Another neighbour said cries for help could be heard from the rooftop as the fire intensified. Police said a PCR call about the fire was received at the Govindpuri police station at around 2.31 am. Soon after, officials began rescue operations amid heavy smoke rapidly filling the building. Eight people were rescued and taken to Safdarjung Hospital and AIIMS Trauma Centre for treatment, PTI reported. The deceased were identified as Pankaj (28), his mother Guddi (50), and sister Soni (20), all residents of the third floor. 标题: 一家四代12人 ， 火灾中丧生背后
正文: 2025年12月9日晚，广东省汕头市潮南区峡山街道丹凤路，一栋名为“裕丰五金电器店”的钢筋混凝土结构自建房突发火灾。约40分钟后，明火被扑灭，过火面积约150平方米。 这场火灾夺走了12条生命，遇难者为店主吴某某的家人，包括祖孙四代。该铺面此前的地图街景显示，该栋建筑共4层，一楼为3个门面拉通组合的铺面，楼上3层窗户上皆有防盗窗。   12月9日晚，“裕丰五金电器店”火灾现场。视频截图 此前，当地也有类似事故发生。今年6月，距离此地3公里的西沟市场一铺面火灾造成3人死亡。这个铺面同样是商住混合结构，一层经营粮食销售，二层为居住阁楼。后来，广东省安全生产委员会办公室对该起事故查处实行挂牌督办。 这样的自建房在国内并不少见，通常被称为“三合一”或“多合一”场所——即在同一空间内，同时存在住宿、生产、经营或仓储等多种功能。今年7月，国家消防救援局相关负责人曾在新闻发布会上表示，2025年上半年，经营性小场所发生较大火灾8起，亡人率同比上升39.5％。经营性小场所普遍规模不大，但不少存在经营、储存、居住“三合一”现象，“下店上宅”“前店后宅”现象，是引发火灾伤亡的重要原因。 中国消防科普委员会专家委员、消防安全科普博主刘祖河刚刚完成对汕头这起事故的现场调研。他告诉《中国新闻周刊》，对小本经营者而言，“下店上宅”等自建房能极大程度压缩生计成本，兼顾经营便利与家庭照看，但由于此类建筑大多未经正规设计、审批和施工监理，从建造之初便埋下了安全隐患。 “天然的温床” 还未靠近丹凤路，广东省汕头市大宅村居民李盛听到急促的消防警报声由远及近持续鸣响。他意识到，附近出事了。 沿着惯常路线，他骑行至丹凤路。前方路口已被警方封锁。时间接近12月9日22时，火势已基本被扑灭，一楼的商铺内仍有零星火光闪烁，而二楼以上的部分则完全陷入黑暗。整栋四层建筑的外墙被浓烟熏得漆黑一片。 在救援现场，李盛看到有十几辆消防车聚集，其中包括从邻近和平镇调派的车辆，两辆救护车闪烁着顶灯，守候在侧。消防员和医护人员主要从建筑的后门进出，不断有人被救援人员用担架抬出，并迅速送往停靠在后门附近的救护车。 据悉，事发地点位于潮南区峡山街道丹凤路裕丰五金电器店。工商登记信息显示，该店成立于2010年，经营者为吴某某，主要销售家用电器、电机和五金工具。李盛也对《中国新闻周刊》表示，在他的印象中，该店铺一楼放满各类五金商品，是典型的“下店上宅”格局，即一层经营，上层住人。   12月10日，“裕丰五金电器店”所在的4层建筑。图/新华 “下店上宅”等自建房在民营经济活跃、自建房密集的沿海一带普遍存在。在中国消防救援学院青年教师周静看来，绝大多数此类建筑有着先天安全缺陷。许多建于十几年甚至二十几年前的自建房，当时的报建程序可能仅是“跟村委会说一声”，设计、材料与现行建筑防火规范相去甚远，变成“历史遗留问题”。 王峰是一位拥有15年从业经验的国家一级注册建筑师，长期承接各类乡村自建房项目，他解释称，现行《建筑设计防火规范》对此类建筑有明确规定，比如：商业与居住部分必须采用耐火极限高的实体墙进行分隔，且在这道防火墙上原则上不应开设门窗洞口；必须为商业部分设置独立的安全出口；需设置便于消防救援的窗口等设施。“也就是更应注重防止火灾对上部住宅部分产生影响。”王峰总结道。 而对于那些建造时间已久、不符合新规的“下店上宅”自建房，刘祖河形容为“天然的温床”。他说，此类场所因经营或仓储区域可燃物高度集中，火灾风险极高，而且火灾发展速度往往超乎常人想象，“从一点小火苗演变成完全失控的大火，仅仅需要三分钟左右”。 “一个垂直的楼梯间就相当于一个烟囱。”刘祖河解释道，这类建筑的构造缺陷在于，连接楼下经营与楼上居住空间的，通常只有一部内部楼梯。一旦楼下起火，高温、浓烟和有毒气体沿楼梯急速上蹿，迅速吞噬唯一的逃生通道，留给楼上居民的反应时间和逃生空间都极为有限。 对于消防救援人员，此类火场同样是严峻挑战。刘祖河分析，救援难点是多方面的，首先，火情发展迅猛，救援人员到达现场时往往已处于猛烈燃烧阶段，内部充满高温浓烟，能见度极低；其次，建筑功能复杂，货物堆积情况不明，搜救人员需要在危险环境中快速定位被困者，而“有些是自己搭的夹层，人在阁楼里”，结构隐蔽，增加了搜寻难度。 他进一步解释，在此类场所，如果盲目破门强攻，射水灭火时产生的水蒸气与压力，可能会将高温烟气逼向被困者藏身的位置，反而加剧其生存风险。“这种救援是很困难的，需要非常谨慎的判断和战术配合。” 发现起火后，周边邻居第一时间自发用消防栓灭火 “蒙混过关” 事实上，“下店上宅”的安全风险，并非无人意识到。多名受访者表示，在基层消防部门，“三合一”场所一直是重点排查对象。但问题在于，整改并不容易。 正文: Condo fire displaces 14 people in Haddonfield; 2 cats killed - A fast-moving fire at Haddonfield Commons left 14 residents homeless just before Thanksgiving, with extensive damage to 12 units, four of which suffered primary fire damage. A fast-moving fire tore through part of the Haddonfield Commons early Thursday morning, leaving 14 residents without a home just a week before Thanksgiving. Smoke and flames were pouring out of the apartment building around 5:30 a.m. when Patrick Samulis said he first noticed something was wrong. "I was getting ready for work, and I started to smell something weird," Samulis said. He lives a few doors down from the unit where the fire began. "I checked out in the hallway, and I heard water running, which I thought was weird. It smelled more like something burning in the hallway, so I ran inside, got the kids said, 'We gotta get out of here, I think there's a fire.' I wasn't even 100% sure at that point," he recalled. Samulis pulled the fire alarm, then rushed with his family to warn neighbors. "These guys got out of bed quick when I said, 'Hey, get up, get up, get up!'" he said, motioning to his three kids. "We went and started banging on some doors, started getting people out, and by that point, you know, we've gone down the stairs and we went outside and we realized the gravity of the situation," he added. His daughter, Anna Samulis, said the scale of the fire was overwhelming. "It was just really shocking," she said. "I didn't expect it to be nearly that large." Everyone inside the building made it out safely, but two cats died in the unit where the bulk of the fire was. "I think they just moved in a week or two prior from another state, Oklahoma, I believe, unfortunately for them. Not a good way to start off," Samulis said. 正文: 1 dead, 14 injured in gas explosion, fire on top floors of New York City apartment building -    Click here to listen to this article  -   Share via - A gas explosion in a Bronx apartment building early Saturday killed one person and injured 14 as firefighters rescued residents in freezing temperatures. - Firefighters were investigating gas odor reports when the explosion struck the 15th and 16th floors, trapping some firefighters in an elevator. - All 148 apartments were evacuated, and the city set up a reception center to assist displaced residents with housing and other needs. NEW YORK — A gas explosion sent fire racing through the top floors of a high-rise apartment building in New York City early Saturday, killing one person and injuring 14 others as temperatures plunged into the single digits overnight, authorities said. Firefighters responded shortly before 12:30 a.m. to the 17-story building in the Bronx, where people were seen leaning out of windows calling for help as flames engulfed parts of the top floors, officials said. Fire chief John Esposito said firefighters were investigating reports of a gas odor on the 15th and 16th floors when the explosion occurred. He said there was major structural damage to about a dozen apartments and fires in 10 apartments on the 16th and 17th floors. Authorities did not immediately release information on the person who died. Another person was critically injured, five had serious injuries and eight had minor injuries, officials said. Officials said the building had been undergoing renovations, and work on the natural gas system had been completed and inspected. The cause of the explosion was under investigation. The building was formerly run by the New York City Housing Authority, but it has been under private management since 2024, city officials said. “It’s an incredible tragedy. 标题: Newport News fire kills 1 , forces 14 from homes
正文: NEWPORT NEWS — Edward “Pops” Stafford was in bed early Sunday when he awoke to his grandson’s voice. “Grandpa, get up! Get up! Get up!” the boy yelled. Stafford, 87, opened the door of his bedroom on 51st Street in the Huntington Heights neighborhood. “Boom, the smoke hit me right in the face,” he said. “And I fell down the steps, because I couldn’t see. I grabbed my grandson, and we ran out of the house right quick.” Stafford and his 45-year-old daughter escaped the home’s second floor during the blaze, as did his daughter’s mother, 70, and Stafford’s two grandchildren, 15 and 11. But another resident — a family friend of the Stafford’s who uses a wheelchair — did not make it out. She was also on the second floor. “We tried,” Stafford said. “But the smoke.” The fire broke out at 1:47 a.m. in the 300 block of 51st Street, within view of the 50th Street gate at Newport News Shipbuilding. Newport News Fire Chief Wesley Rogers said that when firefighters arrived, a man at the scene told them someone was believed to be trapped inside. “Our firefighters made an attempt to make entry into the building,” Rogers said. But they faced heavy heat and smoke. “The fire was so intense that it caused integrity issues with the building,” Rogers said. When firefighters got to the second floor, he said, they felt the floor beneath them starting to give way. “With the amount of heat and fire that they were sustaining, they could not make any further attempt,” Rogers said. He said a decision needed to be made on whether the trapped occupant was likely still alive given the blaze’s intensity. “If there is any chance for us to save an individual in the building, we will absolutely do so,” Rogers said. “And we would risk the lives of our firefighters to do that. 标题: 3 dead , including a child , in explosion at Dallas apartment building
正文: An explosion and massive fire at a Dallas apartment building Thursday killed a child and at least two other people following a blast that shook nearby homes and happened while firefighters were rushing to a reported gas leak, officials said. At least five people also went to hospitals with injuries, Dallas Fire-Rescue spokesperson Jason Evans said. It was unclear how many residents lived in the two-story complex in the Oak Cliff neighborhood south of downtown Dallas, where a towering plume of black smoke was visible for miles. Evans did not rule out that more victims could be found as crews continued to sift through the charred remains of the building. By late Thursday, Evans said firefighters had searched less than half of the scene by hand and that some areas would require excavation. “This was enormous,” Evans said of the fire. As dozens of firefighters swarmed to the neighborhood, some residents’ friends and relatives worried as they tried unsuccessfully to reach each loved ones. Dozens of firefighters searched through the smoldering rubble of the building even as colleagues continued to drench the blackened debris. Berry said firefighters were responding to a call of a gas leak when an explosion happened. “We had the cavalry coming," Dallas Fire-Rescue Deputy Chief Mark Berry said. "But the explosion had already taken place.” Atmos Energy, a natural gas provider, said in a statement they were told by fire officials that a construction crew unrelated to the company had damaged a pipeline near the site of the fire. Kacee Proctor, a resident of the apartment building, said her mother had smelled gas inside a day earlier, but Proctor didn't think much of it at the time. 正文: An Oregon man is behind bars after he yelled racial slurs before setting his apartment building ablaze, leaving two people injured and several others homeless. Shaun Szwarz, 40, now faces six counts each of first-degree arson, reckless endangering, and first-degree criminal mischief for the four-alarm fire at an apartment complex in Portland, Oregon, on July 11. The 40-year-old is accused of setting fire to his unit, which rapidly spread to other parts of the complex, triggering drastic evacuation measures from his neighbors, many of whom had to jump from the apartments on higher floors to escape the intense flames. One neighbor told KATU that the blaze even forced an elderly woman to jump from her balcony. “An 82-year-old lady who jumped off that balcony over there to try to make it out…It’s an insane story,” Michael Jones said. Two people were hospitalized with severe injuries, including third-degree burns, a fractured vertebra, and an ankle injury. The fire severely damaged six of the building’s 19 apartments, making them uninhabitable, and displaced at least 15 people, according to local reports. Jones said that Szwarz even returned to the scene of the crime, making bizarre statements. “The guy had the nerve to come back here and his words: ‘Oh, these are all my Black friends,'” Jones said of the African-American neighbors who were not displaced. “Then police ended up coming to get him.” Jones simply called it “an idiot moment.” Szwarz initially claimed that he was asleep when the fire started, but witness accounts tell a different story. One of his neighbors said he heard Szwarz screaming and yelling racial slurs inside his apartment. Szwarz told investigators that he was arguing on the phone with his girlfriend, but when authorities contacted the woman, she said she had not spoken to Szwarz in two years. 正文: 经济观察报记者 郑晨烨 11月27日凌晨3时57分，香港特区政府发布新闻公报，通报大埔宏福苑五级火警的最新伤亡数据：事故已造成36人死亡，36人受伤，其中7人情况危殆。在确认的死者中，包含一名入职9年的消防队员，仍有279人处于失联状态。 另据最新信息，大埔宏福苑火灾目前已造成44人遇难，45人受伤。香港警方已拘捕3名相关工程公司负责人，包括2名董事、1名工程顾问，年龄介于52岁至68岁。 这场大火始于11月26日下午2时51分，起火点最初位于宏昌阁外墙棚架，随后火势在数小时内迅速蔓延至周边大厦，于当日傍晚6时22分被消防处升级为香港火警分级制度中最高的“五级”。 香港特区行政长官李家超在27日凌晨的记者会上，将此次事件定性为“重大灾难”。 11月27日凌晨1点，经济观察报记者赶抵大埔事发现场。 通往宏福苑的周边道路已被警方实施大范围交通管制，出租车司机告诉记者“附近四十几条路已全部封死”，大量消防车、救护车及警车停满了街道。 虽然警戒线被拉设在距离火场较远的位置，但记者在封锁线外仍能闻到空气中弥漫着浓烈的焦煳味，地面上散落着大量被风吹至此处的、呈黑色的颗粒状崩落物。 透过夜色，记者在现场看到，宏福苑西北方向楼宇的明火已基本熄灭，但东南方向的三栋大厦外立面仍有明火燃烧，部分中高楼层的窗户内透出清晰的红光。 警方在通报中指出，此次火势蔓延速度及程度“不寻常”，目前已联同消防处成立专案组，明确循刑事方向展开全方位调查。 封锁线外，地面上呈黑色的颗粒状崩落物 郑晨烨/摄 11月27日凌晨2点，部分楼栋外立面火势仍明显 郑晨烨/摄 凌晨的大埔 11月27日凌晨1时，经济观察报记者抵达香港大埔宏福苑火灾现场，此时，距离起火已过去逾10个小时。 由于火势仍未完全扑灭，警方在距离事发屋苑数个街区外拉起了多重封锁线。 据现场维持秩序的警员介绍，周边四十多条道路已实施临时交通管制，除救援车辆外，社会车辆一律禁行。 大埔宏福苑外围 郑晨烨/摄 在封锁线外围，记者脚下的柏油路面上散落着大量黑色的颗粒状物体，一位警员告诉记者，这些都是从火场飘落并冷却后的“焦炭”，即被烧毁的建筑外墙残骸。 空气中弥漫着一股刺鼻的、混合着塑料与竹木烧焦的化学气味。 记者在封锁线外看到，整个屋苑的火势呈现出截然不同的两面，西北侧的大厦已经熄灭，隐入黑暗，只留下外墙大面积的熏黑痕迹。 而东南侧的三栋住宅楼，大火仍在持续，火焰不仅在外立面燃烧，更从多个高层单位的窗户内向外喷涌，被烧断的竹棚和杂物带着火星，不断从高空坠落至地面。 在警戒线内，停满了红色的消防车和白色的救护车，车顶的警示灯将街道映成一片红蓝交织的颜色，虽然特区政府通报显示已投入超过1200名消防及救护人员，但在火场核心区，物理条件的限制成为救援的最大掣肘。 记者在现场观察到，尽管多辆配备旋转台钢梯的重型消防车正在作业，但其喷射的水柱仅能覆盖楼宇的中低层区域，对于燃势猛烈的高层单位，地面的水龙明显“鞭长莫及”。 现场一位警务人员向记者确认，受限于现场街道的宽度以及现有消防设备的臂长，水枪和云梯确实难以直接触及顶层火点，目前的作业重点主要是对中层及外墙进行喷淋降温。 在夜空中，有几架隶属于消防处的无人机在被烟雾笼罩的大厦顶部盘旋，进行火场勘察和照明。 在封锁线外，记者遇到了多位已从火场撤离或正在等待消息的宏福苑居民，他们大多神情疲惫，衣着单薄。 一位住在宏昌阁9楼的罗姓居民告诉记者，火灾发生于下午两三点左右。 据他描述，起火点位于大厦底部的外墙棚架，火势是“从下往上”迅速烧起来的。 宏福苑建于1983年，楼龄超过40年，是香港早期的“居者有其屋”计划屋苑，社区内居住着大量长者。一位已经在宏福苑居住了三十多年的老街坊表示，由于大厦楼龄高，很多住户都是行动不便的老人，火灾发生速度之快，让高层住户几乎没有反应时间。 “没有听到警铃响。”这是记者在现场走访时，多位不同楼栋的居民共同提及的一个细节。 上述9楼居民回忆，事发时他并没有听到大厦的火灾警报声。 而他之所以能及时逃生，是因为手机上的社区群组里有人发消息说“着火了”，紧接着邻里之间开始“人传人”地互相通知。另一位逃生者也向记者证实，当时场面一度非常混乱，大家主要靠手机互通消息，或者看到窗外飘落的火星和浓烟才意识到危险迫近。 凌晨2时许，记者来到了位于中华基督教会冯梁结纪念中学的临时庇护中心。 标题: World News : Construction firm bosses held as blaze toll hits 83
正文: Hong Kong police arrested the bosses of a construction company on suspicion of manslaughter yesterday over the city’s worst fire in nearly 80 years, which killed at least 83 people with scores more listed as missing. By early this morning, firemen had mostly contained the blaze raging for more than 24 hours, ripping through the Wang Fuk Court housing complex in the northern district of Tai Po. The estate had been undergoing renovations and was wrapped in bamboo scaffolding and green mesh. Most of the victims were found in two high-rise blocks in the eight-tower complex, Deputy Director of Fire Services Derek Armstrong Chan said. He said firemen found residents who were alive in several of the buildings, but gave no further details. The South China Morning Post reported one survivor was found on the stairwell of one of the buildings. Rescuers battled intense heat, thick smoke and collapsing scaffolding and debris as they fought to reach residents feared trapped on the upper floors of the complex. “We expect the fire to be fully put out tonight,” Chan said. “We’ll continue to douse water to lower the temperatures,” he added. A distraught woman carrying her daughter’s graduation photograph searched for her child outside a shelter, one of eight that authorities said are housing 900 residents. “She and her father are still not out yet,” said the 52-year-old, who gave only her surname, Ng, as she sobbed. “They didn’t have water to save our building.” Police arrested two directors and an engineering consultant of Prestige Construction, a firm contracted to perform maintenance on the buildings. Police said those arrested were under suspicion of manslaughter for using unsafe materials. “We have reason to believe that the company’s responsible parties were grossly negligent, which led to this accident and caused the fire to spread uncontrollably, resulting in major casualties,” Police Superintendent Eileen Chung said. 标题: Thorncliffe Park fire : Toronto fire crews provide update
正文: Multiple charges have been laid in connection with a high-rise fire at a Thorncliffe Park condo that burned for weeks and displaced hundreds of residents late last year. Toronto Fire Chief Jim Jessop announced the charges during a press conference on Thursday afternoon. He said that a construction company, a property management company and the condo corporation are all facing multiple charges under the Ontario Fire Code. How did the fire start? The fire initially began on Nov. 27 during what Jessop described as construction work inside 11 Thorncliffe Park Dr. “The investigation determined that construction activities were being undertaken at 11 Thorncliffe Park Drive whereby ignition sources were used near combustible materials, causing the fire to ignite,” he said. “Toronto Fire Services was not notified of the fire for over 30 minutes.” The blaze quickly grew from a two-alarm call into a five-alarm fire and spread to a neighbouring building at 21 Overlea Blvd., forcing the evacuation of all 408 units across both towers. Jessop said the buildings’ design played a major role in the fire’s spread and longevity. “The buildings are connected to one another by two exterior walls extending vertically from the basement levels through floors one to 10, where the height of 11 Thorncliffe Park Drive ends... Jessop said that the fire burned within concealed spaces between the structures, feeding on combustible materials and making it difficult for crews to access and extinguish. 标题: 香港大埔住宅楼大火延烧的一夜
正文: “火（烧得）特别快，‘呼’就起来了，风一吹，就往楼上冲，烧得‘砰砰’响。” 香港新界大埔屋邨宏福苑多栋住宅楼发生火灾，已造成至少44人遇难，45人受伤。一夜过后，已看不到大面积明火，但火势尚未完全扑灭。 今晨7时30分许，肖南笙看到宏福苑的火仍未熄灭（图/新京报） 视频显示，火势在多栋居民楼迅速蔓延。火灾发生时，建于1983年的宏福苑的居民楼正经历维修。据新华社消息，香港警方展开调查，发现着火建筑物外墙有保护网、防水帆布、塑料布，疑未符合防火标准，另有一座未波及的大厦每层电梯大堂窗外都有发泡胶包封，易燃且可能加速火势蔓延，不排除发泡胶是火势迅速蔓延的原因。 另据中新网报道，香港消防处副处长陈庆勇表示，据初步判断，多处杂物及竹棚在火情中被点燃，并受风势影响飘散到附近大厦，最终火势蔓延至8幢大厦中的7幢。 11月27日凌晨，澎湃新闻记者从深圳皇岗口岸通关进入香港时，距火灾事发地大埔宏福苑近19公里，已能闻到空气中弥漫的焦糊气味。 家离宏福苑仅一街之隔的一名居民回忆说，11月26日下午临近3点，她刚午睡醒来，就在阳台看到宏福苑起火了，“火（烧得）特别快，‘呼’就起来了，风一吹，就往楼上冲，烧得‘砰砰’响”。消防很快赶来，但当时“水只能冲到八楼、十楼（高）”。火烧到傍晚六点，一些高楼外的脚手架已经“渣都不剩了”。 这位居民说，他们一家被烟熏得喘不过气，担心被火势牵连，干脆搬到附近的广福商场打地铺。 住在宏福苑宏仁阁17楼的黎英表示，从她记事的二十多年里，宏福苑很少发生火灾，儿时有次听到邻居家火警钟报警，消防车很快就把火扑灭了。这次起火，她放下手头工作，约下午4点赶到家，小区已拉起警戒线，她所在楼栋“没有被烧到，但也不让进去”。到下午5点多，火势蔓延到了宏仁阁。 27日凌晨两点，记者抵达火灾现场，看到宏福苑周边路段已实施交通管制，消防员正在灭火；靠近小区的人行天桥上，几乎站满驻足观望火情的市民，不时有人因刺鼻烟味咳嗽；天桥下方的双向四车道，挤满随时待命的消防、救护、警车，放眼望去，警灯的红光延伸到了路的尽头。 记者从天桥视角观察到，至少四条水柱喷向火势明显的三栋高楼，滚滚浓烟汇聚空中；其中两栋大楼火势较大，外立墙体黢黑，部分楼层几乎整层充斥灼眼火光，还有火焰冲出窗户跳动。 凌晨4点半，随着一股强风吹过，部分原本即将熄灭的房间火势又起，并伴随“噼啪”响声和杂物坠落声。 在消防队彻夜救援的同时，宏福苑附近的中华基督教会冯梁结纪念中学气氛也比平时更为紧张，在这个临时安置点，热心市民不断扛着成箱的饮用水、干粮涌入，有人则提着大包小包的被褥、毛毯、厚外套。住在元朗区的陈先生说，事发后他挨个给安置点打电话，晚上9点下班后直接开车去采购物资，来来回回已经跑了4个点位运输，“能帮就帮，公民责任”。 收到物资后，香港义工团队“爱心队”在校内未做停歇，一名队员介绍说，本次支援队伍共19人，都是得知灾情后从香港各区自发赶来。凌晨3点，他们和市民忙着把成堆的饮用水和食品分开摞齐，好留出通道分发物资。其间，一些人前往广福商场为露宿居民发放被褥、暖贴和水。 现场的救援物资（红星新闻现场视频截图） 受此次火灾影响，宏福苑小区及周边紧邻楼栋居民被暂时疏散，其中一些人选择在广福商场二层的露天广场过夜，那儿可以看到火情，有的人裹着毛毯，着火的高楼他们眼中映出火光，有人一盯就是一整晚。其中便有家在宏福苑宏志阁28楼的张女士，26日下午4点，她刷到火灾新闻后立马给60多岁的母亲打了电话，母亲告诉她，外边黑烟太大，跑屋里了，出不去，只能关紧门等救援。“当时好像火还没烧到我家那栋楼”，等她报了警赶到家，楼已起火，之后，她没能再拨通母亲的电话。 更多人席地而睡，亦或枕靠在长椅、石柱旁。一位老人拿毛毯蒙住了头，睡得正沉的她身体歪斜，一只手漏出毯子了，上面的皱纹被暖黄路灯照得格外清晰。 62岁的李阿超没睡，背靠椅子坐久了，便俯身把身体重心撑在雨伞上缓解腰酸，或揉揉劳损过度的膝关节。他是名清洁工，家紧挨着宏福苑，26日凌晨他上完晚班就到广场坐着了，带着个小布袋，装着水、两个桃子、一板还剩一颗的止痛药。妻儿都去了室内安置点，他不去，“我就要在这儿坐着”。 11月27日早上8点，经消防队彻夜灭火，少数楼层房间内部有火焰跳动，现场高楼浓烟减退，至12点，火势基本得到控制。 此次火灾为何如此凶猛？ 据南方都市报报道，有业内人士分析，此次香港大埔的五级火警，其扑救难点主要源于高层建筑“立体燃烧”的复杂性。火势在拥有40余年楼龄的旧楼外墙棚架上迅速蔓延，形成“烟囱效应”，加之强风天气，导致灭火难度极大。 11月26日拍摄的火灾救援现场（图/新华社） 标题: Firefighters control blaze near Dubai Mall of the Emirates
正文: A fire broke out in a residential building near Mall of the Emirates in Dubai's Al Barsha area on Tuesday. Emergency services were at the scene in six minutes, after receiving news of the incident at 2pm, Dubai Media Office reported. The blaze was successfully controlled, with no casualties reported. "Dubai Civil Defence teams have fully brought under control a fire that broke out today in a residential building in the Al Barsha area," a statement said on X. Deputy shift commander Reshef Tomer Kashri said crews encountered heavy smoke coming from a second-floor unit in a 12-story building. “Upon arrival, we noticed black smoke coming from the second floor of a 12-story building,” Kashri said. “We forced open the entrance door and saw electric bicycles completely engulfed in flames. Firefighters began conducting searches and extinguishing the source of the fire. The apartment’s residents were trapped in separate rooms. We rescued five residents. One was in serious condition and the others were lightly injured. They were transferred to MDA for treatment.” Fire officials reiterate safety guidance Emergency operators from the Dan District’s 102 center remained in continuous contact with those trapped inside the apartment, instructing them to stay sheltered in place throughout the incident until firefighters reached them. A fire investigator was called to the scene to examine the circumstances surrounding the blaze. Fire officials used the incident to reiterate safety guidance, urging the public to install smoke detectors, which they described as inexpensive, easy to install, and life-saving by providing early warning that allows residents to escape in time. They also warned against charging lithium batteries unattended and stressed that building entrances must never be blocked, particularly when storing items such as electric bicycles. The cause of the fire remains under investigation.

标题: Gas explosion causes partial collapse of high - rise apartment building in New Y
正文: The city's fire department said it had no immediate reports of injuries. NEW YORK -- A gas explosion in an apartment building in the Bronx caused a partial collapse Wednesday morning, leaving a corner of the building a pile of rubble. City police said they received 911 calls about a building collapse just after 8 a.m. Wednesday at the Mitchel Houses building. "Upon arrival, officers observed a partial building collapse," police said in a statement. The city's fire department said it had no immediate reports of injuries. It said it was responding to a report of a gas explosion that collapsed an incinerator shaft in the building in the Bronx. The rest of the building appeared to be stable with no apartments affected, but that was being investigated by the Department of Buildings. The building is city-owned public housing. Multiple messages seeking comment were left with the Housing Authority. Video from the scene shows a high-rise with one corner collapsed from the ground floor to the roof. Videos by nearby residents showed a cloud of dust billowing over the block moments after the collapse. Mayor Eric Adams said he was briefed about the emergency and officials were still getting a full assessment. "Please avoid the area for your safety," he wrote on X. Incinerator shafts in New York City buildings were once used to dispose of trash, which was then burned on site. But they have largely been replaced with trash compactors, which can use the same chutes. In July 2023, a towering construction crane caught fire high above the West Side of Manhattan, causing its long arm to snap off, smash against a nearby building and plummet to the street as people ran for their lives on the sidewalk below. Several people suffered minor injuries in the collapse, but no one died. The Associated Press and WABC contributed to this report.

正文: A fatal mistake by a young woman in South Korea, attempting to kill a cockroach, led to a devastating fire that claimed the life of her neighbor. The victim, a Chinese woman in her 30s, lived on the fifth floor with her husband and two-month-old baby. When they noticed the fire, they opened their window and called for help. They managed to pass their baby to a neighbor in a nearby building through the window. The husband escaped by climbing across, but his wife fell as she tried to follow. She was rushed to hospital but died hours later from her injuries. Police believe the couple attempted to flee through the window because smoke blocked the building’s staircase. The structure houses commercial shops on the ground floor and 32 apartments above. Eight other residents suffered respiratory issues due to smoke inhalation. Police in Osan, north of Seoul, said the suspect may face charges of negligent arson and involuntary manslaughter. In recent years, the trend of using flame devices or homemade flamethrowers to kill cockroaches has gained popularity on social media despite its extreme danger. 正文: 近日 广东省中山市三乡镇某小区 17层住宅凌晨发生火灾 消防部门接警后迅速到场处置 所幸着火住宅及相邻住宅的住户 接受过消防安全培训 在火灾发生时科学逃生自救 火灾并未造成人员伤亡 起火原因正在进一步调查当中 事发时 他们做对了什么？ 发现火情，及时报警 据了解，着火住宅屋主发现起火后，立即叫醒家人，当发现无法自行扑灭火灾后，众人便疏散到地面并报警求助。消防员到场后迅速展开行动，攻坚小组利用室内消火栓铺设水带，压制火势蔓延；搜救小组对着火楼层及相邻楼层展开搜救，在起火住宅对面的住宅发现一名被困住户，随即护送其沿疏散楼梯安全撤离至地面。 浓烟关门，固守待援 被困住户向消防员表示，在发现火情且楼梯间充满烟气后，她并没有慌乱逃窜，而是立即关闭房门，用湿毛巾堵住门缝，防止浓烟侵入，并用手机向外界发送求救信息。这一系列正确的自救行为，为自身安全脱险争取了宝贵时间。 冷静判断，捂口鼻有序撤离 住宅上层另有6名群众察觉楼下着火后，发现浓烟尚未充满楼梯间，且能见度正常，6人捂住口鼻，沿着疏散楼梯有序向下撤离，安全脱离险境。 高层建筑火灾 有这些危险性↓ 1.火险隐患多 高层建筑，特别是综合性的高层建筑，功能复杂，可燃物多，消防安全管理不严，火险隐患多，火灾危险性大。特别是火灾中产生烟雾和毒气，对生命安全造成很大威胁。 2.火势蔓延快 高层建筑一般室内可燃物较多，有的高层住宅建筑还违规设置可燃物品库房，一旦起火，燃烧猛烈，容易蔓延。 3.安全疏散困难 多数高层建筑安全疏散主要靠楼梯，但由于层数多，垂直距离长，疏散到地面或其他安全场所的时间也相对较长，且楼梯间内一旦窜入烟气，就会严重影响疏散。 4.扑救难度大 高层建筑高达几十米，甚至数百米，一旦室内消防设施不能正常发挥作用，从室外进行扑救相当困难。 如果要想成功逃生 很多时候要靠自救 这些大家要记牢 往上跑，还是往下跑？ 楼下起火 如楼梯间有浓烟 千万不要盲目通过楼梯间逃生 楼上起火 要往楼下跑 家外面着火 应第一时间判断起火点、火势大小 选择相应的逃生路线 出口被浓烟大火封住怎么办？ 如果出口被浓烟或者是大火给堵住不能安全穿越时，应该选择在目前的楼层关门避难，而不是往上或往下跑。切记，关上房门，用湿毛巾封堵门缝，迅速拨打119等待救援！ 眼下正值冬春季节 用火用电用气量增加 火灾隐患增多 消防安全不容小觑 这些安全细节要留心↓ （来源：中华人民共和国应急管理部、央视新闻客户端） 特别声明：以上内容(如有图片或视频亦包括在内)为自媒体平台“网易号”用户上传并发布，本平台仅提供信息存储服务。 Notice: The content above (including the pictures and videos if any) is uploaded and posted by a user of NetEase Hao, which is a social media platform and only provides information storage services.

标题: 加州房子离奇爆炸 ， 多名儿童光着脚逃了出来
正文: 周日（11月16日）下午，奇诺岗（Chino Hills）一栋房子在毫无预警之下突然爆炸，随后引发火灾。 据当地邻居表示，爆炸后许多人从房子里逃了出来，其中有几个小孩，有的没穿鞋就跑了出来，一些邻居帮着把孩子送去医院抢救。 据初步统计，一共有8人受伤，经过抢救都没有生命危险。 根据圣贝纳迪诺县警方通报，爆炸发生下午3 点 45 分左右，地点位于奇诺岗塞拉维斯塔大道（ Sierra Vista Drive ） 4222 号，由于是周日，许多人都在家里忙自己的事，突然传出一声巨响。 附近房屋窗户被震碎，车道上的多辆车辆被飞溅的碎片覆盖，甚至还能看到玩具泰迪熊被掀落在车顶，显示爆炸冲击强烈程度。 “突然，我听到一声巨响，听起来就像炸弹爆炸一样。”邻居安德鲁·胡因（ Andrew Huynh ）描述当时的震撼瞬间，“过了几秒的沉默，就听到汽车警报声、尖叫声，到处都是碎片。” 胡因表示，他看到对面房子的一家人抱着孩子逃出来，宠物狗也在街上狂奔。“火势开始往外蔓延，情况变得非常危险。”他说。 另一位邻居表示，她们看到受害者（其中一些是孩子）从烧毁的房屋中跑出来。 “他们当时就大声呼救，说着‘哎哟！好痛！救命！’你知道，他们光着脚，穿着睡衣。小男孩没穿上衣，只穿着运动裤。情况很危急，”一位目击者说道“他们的头发被烧焦了，脸上沾满了血迹。” 原因 疑似天然气爆炸 根据圣贝纳迪诺县警方表示，爆炸发生时屋内一共有8名受害者，有一半的人被急救车送去医院，另外一位邻居将一些年轻的受害者送去了医院，目前均没有生命危险。 根据网上流传的事故照片显示，爆炸后的房屋正面几乎完全被烧毁。外墙焦黑、屋顶塌陷，火舌甚至蔓延至邻近围栏，整个街区弥漫着刺鼻的烟味。 圣贝纳迪诺县警长办公室和奇诺谷消防局接警后迅速赶到现场，与燃气公司协调切断燃气、控制火势，并对周围住户进行紧急疏散。 奇诺谷消防局局长乔恩·克里普（Jon Cripe）表示，现场救援人员到达后立即检测到燃气泄漏。“目前我们已疏散 16 户居民。燃气公司已到达现场，我们正在合作隔离燃气并继续控制紧急状况。”克里普说。 邻居不满 邻居称该住户“问题不断” 虽然官方初步判断爆炸与煤气泄漏有关，但确切原因仍在调查。 然而，许多邻居向媒体透露，他们对这栋房屋发生事故一点也不惊讶——原因是那里“长期出问题”。 邻居艾德琳·阿尔瓦雷斯（Adrienne Alvarez）表示，她很少在白天看到屋内的居民，但曾亲眼见到社会服务人员多次上门。“他们一直都有问题。”她说。 另一位邻居胡因证实，过去一两周警方多次到过该物业，“警察这几天来这里不止一次，每次都一样，他们拘留一些人，但从没发生真正的改变。然后突然之间，这房子就爆炸了。” 有住户表示，社区一直担心该住宅内可能存在违法活动，但目前尚无官方证实。 目前，具体情况还在调查之中。

标题: 刻不容缓 ！ 一场与时间赛跑的紧急救援 -- 中国警察网
正文: 10月23日凌晨，按照安徽省马鞍山市公安局花山分局常态化夜间巡防部署，绿地警务站民警潘小虎与辅警张文龙沿朝霞路开展巡逻值守。行至某居民小区附近时，潘小虎凭借多年夜巡积累的敏锐洞察力，发现临街一栋高层住宅楼20多层处有异常火光闪烁。 因高层建筑遮挡，无法锁定起火楼层，二人当即分工：潘小虎前往小区，同步向上级详细汇报火情位置、现场火势等实时动态；张文龙紧随其后，在小区入口做好秩序维护与引导准备。 “不确定火源，就从20层开始逐层排查！”面对紧急态势，二人迅速敲定方案，沿楼梯从20层开始逐层向上排查。随着排查推进，空气中的焦糊味愈发浓烈。当二人排查至25层时，一股刺鼻浓烟从一户居民家门缝渗出，起火点找到了！ 潘小虎一边向指挥中心上报起火点准确地址，请求支援警力及消防力量紧急驰援，一边与张文龙轮番用力敲打起火住户房门。“屋里有人吗？着火了，快开门！”急促的呼叫声与敲门声在空旷的楼道内回荡，屋内却始终无人回应。 因房门为加固结构，二人尝试撬动、撞击均无法打开。情况愈发紧急，潘小虎继续在门外呼喊提醒，张文龙则迅速逐户敲门，引导25层及以上住户有序向楼下安全区域疏散。 随后，花山分局特巡警大队、霍里派出所警力接到指挥中心支援指令后迅速响应，火速抵达现场，共同疏导住户30余人，并同步引导消防救援车、120急救车顺利入场。很快，消防救援力量与120急救人员相继赶到。 消防救援人员使用破拆工具打开起火房门，浓烟与热浪瞬间涌出。消防救援人员迅速展开灭火救援，仅用10分钟便成功控制住火势，并救出被困在卧室内的谷先生一家四口，其中包括一名年仅1岁的幼儿。经120急救人员初步检查，4人虽吸入少量浓烟，但意识清醒，随后被紧急送往医院做进一步观察。 “当晚家中用电饭锅炖煮排骨后忘记关闭电源，全家睡着后未察觉异常，连门外的救援呼喊和敲门声都没听见。”事后，谷先生回忆事发经过时仍心有余悸。参与救援的消防救援人员表示，凌晨时段是居民熟睡、安全防范意识最薄弱的时期，若火情未被及时发现，待火势与浓烟大范围蔓延后，极可能造成无法挽回的后果。睡前要仔细检查相关电器、煤气灶是否关闭。 据悉，花山分局科学规划16条夜间警力必巡路线，在重点商圈、居民小区、交通要道设置12个必守点位，通过“定点值守+动态巡逻”的常态化模式，全力守护群众安全。 “花山分局通过夜间巡防工作筑牢辖区治安防线，全力守护群众生命财产安全。”花山分局副局长张阅表示。据统计，今年以来，该局通过夜间巡防累计及时发现并处置各类安全隐患146起，协助侦破案件149起，为群众办实事、解难题890余次。

标题: Survivors of South Africa's horrific building fire now live in fear of guns - BBC
正文:
Blackened by soot, the gutted and derelict remains of South Africa's infamous Usindiso building in central Johannesburg are an unintentional memorial to the 76 people who died here in a devastating fire two years ago.
At one time an office block, the 1950s building in the Marshalltown area was abandoned and then taken over by several hundred people desperately needing a home.
One of those was Vusi Tshabalala, who shakes his head in disbelief as he recalls how he survived the blaze on that late August night.
"The fire seemed to come out of nowhere," the 45-year-old tells the BBC in a melancholic voice, raspy from years of smoking cigarettes.
Mr Tshabalala was asleep on the third floor of the five-storey building, where he was sharing a place with his then-girlfriend and brother.
Awoken by the flames, they managed to escape by covering themselves in wet blankets and running in the dark towards an exit at the rear.
"As we were running others got injured, because when they fell down, they couldn't get back up. People were running over them. I thank God that we came out without any injuries."
The tragedy shocked the nation and highlighted the deep housing inequalities in Africa's wealthiest city - inequalities the authorities promised to address.
Visiting just hours after the blaze, President Cyril Ramaphosa called it "a wake-up call to begin to address the situation of housing in the inner city".
"We need to find effective ways to deal with the issue of housing," he said.
But two years on, Mr Tshabalala and many others have still not found a permanent home.
Initially he was relocated to Rosettenville, 5km (three miles) south of Marshalltown, but he says he left because he could not find work around there.
Next he tried the industrial neighbourhood of Denver, 6km east of the Usindiso building, where other survivors have been placed - but says the frequent shootings forced him to leave.

标题: El voraz incendio que consumió un edificio de 14 plantas en la ciudad española de Valencia y dejó al menos 10 muertos - BBC
正文:
Al menos 10 personas murieron en un voraz incendio que en pocas horas arrasó por completo este jueves un edificio de viviendas en la ciudad española de Valencia.
Según la prensa local, cuatro de las víctimas eran miembros de una misma familia: el padre, la madre, una niña de 3 años y un recién nacido.
La policía científica encontró este sábado el cádaver de una persona que estaba desaparecida, con lo que la cifra de víctimas mortales asciende a 10. Las autoridades han confirmado que la cifra de desaparecidos coinciden con las de cadáveres, pero que los datos son provisionales hasta que terminen las labores de inspección.
El incendio comenzó el jueves alrededor de las 17:00 hora local (16:00 GMT) en el octavo piso de un edificio del barrio del Campanar de la tercera ciudad más grande de España y luego se propagó rápidamente, avivado por el viento que sopla en la zona.
Algunos expertos dijeron que el edificio estaba cubierto con un revestimiento de poliuretano altamente inflamable, lo que podría explicar la rápida propagación, aunque las autoridades aún no se han pronunciado al respecto.
En el momento del incendio, Valencia estaba experimentando ráfagas de viento de hasta 60 kilómetros por hora, según la oficina meteorológica nacional Aemet.
Un hombre que vivía en el segundo piso del edificio le dijo al canal de televisión La Sexta que las llamas avanzaron rápidamente. "El fuego se propagó en cuestión de 10 minutos", señaló.
El bloque, que estaba compuesto por dos torres unidas de 138 apartamentos, amaneció este viernes completamente calcinado y sobre él se elevan todavía pequeñas columnas de humo.
Los videos del suceso muestran las viviendas siendo consumidas por las llamas y grandes nubes de humo negro envolviendo la construcción.
Las escenas más dramáticas se produjeron mientras los bomberos utilizaban una grúa para sacar a un padre y a su hija de un balcón donde estaban atrapados en una operación retransmitida en directo por la televisión nacional.

标题: What led to hotel fire disaster at Turkish ski resort? - BBC
正文:
The fire that killed 78 people at the Grand Kartal Hotel in the early hours of Monday is one of the deadliest disasters of its kind in Turkish history.
Some survivors have said they did not hear an alarm and experts have told the BBC they would not have expected such a high death toll in a hotel where fire protection systems were working properly.
The 12-storey hotel at Turkey's popular Kartalkaya ski resort hosts tens of thousands of visitors every year, so Turks understandably want to know how such a terrible tragedy could have happened at the start of a two-week school holiday.
The interior minister said the fire started at 03:27 (00:27 GMT) in the restaurant area on the fourth floor and firefighters arrived within 45 minutes.
Some survivors have described smelling smoke as much as an hour earlier.
Culture and Tourism minister Mehmet Nuri Ersoy said the hotel had a fire competence certificate "issued by the fire department".
But that has been challenged by local mayor Tanju Ozcan, who said the fire department had not issued a positive report since 2007.
Some survivors say they heard no alarm, while there have been claims of inadequacies in the hotel's fire extinguishing systems.
"My wife smelled the fire," said Atakan Yelkovan, who said he was staying on the third floor of the hotel.
"We went down earlier than others. The alarm did not go off... It took about an hour to an hour-and-a-half for the fire brigade to come. In the meantime, the fourth and fifth floors were burning. People on the upper floors were screaming."
Some guests on higher floors tried to escape with their bedding and some jumped to their deaths.
Eylem Senturk said the fire alarm did not go off until she was out of the building. Her husband had to jump off the hotel porch because of the smoke: "We are very lucky to have survived."

标题: 'It was terrifying': Residents evacuate after Marina building fire
正文:
A massive fire broke out late Friday night in a 67-storey residential and commercial tower in Dubai Marina, forcing hundreds of residents to evacuate and find shelter. While some waited outside as firefighters battled the blaze, others checked into nearby hotels or took refuge at friends’ homes.
Many residents said fire alarms didn’t go off and they had no idea there was a fire in the building until they smelled smoke or got calls from friends. Thick smoke made stairwells unusable for some, forcing them to rely on elevators to escape. Several residents spent the entire night outdoors before securing temporary shelter.
“I was on the 24th floor with my wife when we started smelling something like burning wires around 9:45 pm,” said one resident. “We checked everything inside the apartment, including the kitchen, but found nothing.
"When we stepped onto the balcony, we saw fire crews arriving and people gathering outside. That’s when we got a call from a friend who was visiting us that he wasn’t allowed in because of a fire. Still, there was no alarm, no official notice. Only when we called building security did they tell us to evacuate," he added.

标题: 广州一居民楼9楼突发火情，他们科学避险成功获救
正文:
据广州消防6月28日通报，6月27日，广州市荔湾区石围塘街道芳村大道西一住宅9楼发生火灾。得益于被困居民科学自救与消防救援部门的快速响应、高效处置，3名被困群众全部成功救出，无生命危险。另有一名群众在消防到场前已自行逃生脱险。
6月27日6时13分，广州市消防救援支队接警后立即调派荔湾大队全勤指挥组及属下5个消防救援站、1个微型消防站，共16辆消防车、63名消防员赶赴现场处置，支队全勤指挥部遂行出动。6时19分，塞坝路消防站率先到场，全程仅用6分钟。到场后，消防员迅速研判现场火情，即刻开展内攻灭火、人员搜救工作。
经过紧急处置，现场明火于7时11分被彻底扑灭。7时20分，三名被困群众全部成功救出。经查，起火建筑为钢筋混凝土结构住宅，共10层，着火部位为910房，建筑面积约90平方米，主要燃烧物为家具等。目前，火灾原因正在进一步调查中。
消防部门透露，起火住宅为复式阁楼结构。事发时一家人均在睡梦中，35岁的女事主最先察觉火情，当即告知阁楼上的老人与11岁女孩起火，让她们佩戴防烟面罩在安全位置等待救援，自己则寻找逃生路线。老人和孩子听到后，按照其叮嘱，戴上防烟面罩退至10楼阳台通风处固守待援。
女事主试图从入户门及其他通道逃生，均因9楼已全面过火、烟火猛烈冲入各房间而失败，最终被困在自家房间内。无奈之下，她打开窗户翻出，沿外墙攀爬至邻居909室的空调外机上，等待救援。
与此同时，其丈夫在卧室听到动静后开门查看，发现火势猛烈，当即关闭房门退至窗台，拆除防盗网沿外墙进入9楼楼梯间，成功自行撤离至楼外。一家人科学、规范的初期自救操作，最大程度规避了伤亡风险，也为消防后续专业救援争取了宝贵时间。
消防救援人员抵达现场侦查后，快速锁定三名被困人员的具体位置——老人和女孩在10楼阳台，女事主悬在9楼外墙空调外机上，当即分组、同步开展救援作业。
一组消防员携带防毒面罩攀至10楼楼顶，向阳台上的老人和女孩精准抛投防护面罩，并指导她们规范佩戴，有效隔绝有毒浓烟，同时安排消防员在阳台全程安抚被困群众，叮嘱她们固守待援，稳定其情绪；另一组消防员架设2支水枪深入9楼着火区域压制明火，同时延伸1支水枪至10楼，对向上蔓延的烟火进行降温控火，阻断火势二次蔓延。
在全面排查火情、确认现场环境安全，具备人员转移条件后，救援人员迅速组建三人专项救助小组，有序开展人员转移工作。
由于楼梯通道狭窄，仅容单人通行，救援组先将女孩安全转移至楼下，随后折返至10楼阳台，由一名消防员正面抱起老人，将其护送至9楼楼梯口，再由其他消防员接力转移至一楼安全区域。
另一组3名消防员密切配合，一人以安全绳绑定自身腰带与被困人员身体做好高空防护，一人清理窗边杂物打通救援通道，一人用铁铤破拆防盗网开辟出入口，最终成功将被困于909室空调外机处的女事主安全救下。
“家中常年配备防烟面罩等消防器材，自己和家人也经常参加消防安全培训，才能在紧急关头保持冷静、做出正确判断。”事后，男事主向消防部门表示。
“火场逃生谨记‘小火快跑，浓烟关门’。此次被困人员能成功化险为夷，再次印证了消防安全知识和技能储备的重要性。”消防部门提醒广大市民，在日常生活中掌握必备的消防安全知识和技能至关重要，请时刻提高警惕，提升自防自救能力。建议家庭常备防烟面罩、灭火器等消防器材并掌握正确使用方法。高层建筑发生火灾时，若逃生通道被浓烟封堵，应果断关闭门窗、用湿布堵住门缝、退至通风阳台或窗边等待救援，切勿盲目冲入浓烟。家中安装防盗网应预留逃生出口。

标题: People climb across balconies to escape four-story rental house fire in Ho Chi Minh City
正文:
Translated from Vietnamese and summarized by DistantNews. Read the original for the full story.
Several people escaped a four-story rental house in Gò Vấp by climbing across neighboring balconies after a fire filled the building with thick black smoke.
Residents in an alley on Quang Trung Street discovered the smoke and a burning smell coming from the ground floor at about 8 a.m. on July 21. The area was experiencing a power outage at the time. Neighbors tried to attack the flames with small fire extinguishers, but the fire quickly intensified because the house contained many flammable items.
The smoke blocked the ground-floor entrances. A resident said people on the upper floors ran to the balconies in panic and climbed across to adjacent homes before reaching the ground safely.
Ho Chi Minh City police fire and rescue units sent specialized vehicles and dozens of officers to the scene. Firefighters used water hoses from the front of the building while searching the upper floors for anyone trapped. They brought the fire fully under control and stopped it spreading to nearby homes. No one died, but much of the property inside was destroyed. Authorities sealed off the scene and are investigating the cause.
The thick black smoke completely blocked the main entrance on the ground floor. Hearing people shout, those on the upper floors panicked and ran to the balconies, then quickly climbed across to neighboring houses to get safely down to the ground.

标题: 楼下起火,31楼住户冲进浓烟逃生:他们赌对了吗（案例引述西安与南充两起）
正文:
先来看以下案例——2024年1月16日，四川南充一高层住宅27楼突发火灾，住在31楼的邓女士一家在半小时后察觉火情后，做出了一个可怕的决定：打开房门，冲进浓烟，硬是从31楼冲下了楼。虽然最终保住了性命，但全家人均进了医院。
火灾中的浓烟含有大量有毒气体，如一氧化碳、氰化氢、氯化氢等。一氧化碳与血红蛋白的结合能力是氧气的200-250倍，即使吸入少量也会导致意识模糊、昏迷甚至死亡。现代建筑中的塑料制品、合成材料燃烧产生的毒性更强，往往在火势蔓延前就已使人中毒，丧失逃生能力。
火灾烟气的温度极高，一旦吸入会立即灼伤呼吸道黏膜，导致组织水肿、窒息死亡。
浓烟中能见度几乎为零，即使在熟悉的楼道里也很难辨别方向。31层的楼梯，相当于要经过近500级台阶，在黑暗和浓烟中极易踩空或迷失方向。
高层建筑的楼梯间往往形成“烟囱效应”，成为浓烟和火势快速蔓延的通道。实验表明，烟气在楼梯间的垂直扩散速度可达每秒3-4米，意味着只需短短几十秒，整栋楼的疏散通道就可能被有毒烟气充满。
现场视频画面显示，当这家人拧开31楼的房门，黑色的浓烟瞬间涌进客厅。他们抱着孩子，穿着衣服就往浓烟里冲——这简直是在拿生命打赌。
真的要庆幸他们能逃出来，但这样的运气并非人人都有。或许顺利逃出生天，有以下几个偶然因素发挥了作用：
1.楼道内烟气还不是特别大，湿毛巾起了作用：邓女士母亲准备了湿毛巾，自己则用打湿的浴巾捂住小孩的口鼻。
4.楼梯间内的防烟系统运转正常，排烟窗正常开启，排出了一部分烟雾，使得浓度没到“致命级别”，烟气浓度变低。
2023年1月25日19时19分，广东湛江一自建住宅楼发生火灾。起火部位位于该住宅楼梯的1层至2层转角中间平台位置。事故造成4人在逃生过程中死亡（2名老人、2名儿童）。死亡的4人均是7层楼住户，发生火灾后没有冷静分析风险，盲目向下逃生，导致距离起火点越来越近，在楼梯内吸入大量有毒高温烟气，导致抢救无效死亡。
2025年9月，浙江嘉兴一小区内，家住6楼的谢某突然闻到一股浓烈的烟味，打开门查看时，发现楼道里烟气弥漫，还隐约能看到火光闪烁，他意识到是楼下起火，立刻冲回屋内采取自救措施。“快！拿湿毛巾…都到阳台去”谢某到阳台后迅速关上房门，一边开窗，一边安抚三个孩子情绪，同时拨打119报警等待救援。消防员抵达现场后将被困人员救出。本案例中，谢某一直保持冷静，发现楼道烟雾烟气弥漫，没有盲目逃生，而是紧闭房门，用湿毛巾堵住门缝固守待援，最终成功获救。
这种情况极其危险，很多人就是在这种情况下盲目逃生而不幸丧生。这种情况下逃与不逃，主要是开门看烟。
开一条门缝如果有大量浓烟涌入，说明走廊和楼梯间充满了浓烟，这时就要退回室内关门防烟等救援；
如果开门走廊里没有烟，但是楼梯间里有烟，仍然要退回室内关门等待救援；
这种情况危险较小，火在上面，人在下面，火势和浓烟被楼板阻隔，不容易威胁到我们的安全。我们只要从楼梯下楼即可，下楼时不要乘坐电梯。
这种情况相对危险。如何决定逃还是不逃，主要看烟雾情况。我们可开一条门缝，如果门外没有浓烟，就赶紧下楼；
如果火势把通向入户门的路线给封住了，实在是穿不过去，应该找一个有外窗的卫生间或者房间，关门堵缝，做好防烟，等待救援。

A loud boom rattled the office and the north tower started to sway as American Airlines Flight 11 crashed just floors above them.

Roselle remained calm. Side by side, the two made their way to the stairwell where a nightmare scenario awaited.

SINGAPORE - One person was taken to hospital after a fire broke out in a Bukit Panjang flat early on Jan 14.
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) was alerted at around 3.55am to a blaze at Block 501 Jelapang Road. The fire originated among the contents of a bedroom in a fifth-floor unit.
SCDF told The Straits Times that its personnel had to forcibly enter the flat to tackle the fire, which they extinguished using a water jet.
About 100 residents self-evacuated from the block before SCDF arrived. In addition to the individual taken to hospital, SCDF paramedics assessed four others for minor injuries. They declined further medical attention and chose not to be taken to hospital.
The cause of the fire is under investigation by the authorities.
A 75-year-old retiree who lives below the affected flat told Shin Min Daily News that he was awakened by noises.
He was initially confused but realised the situation was serious when he heard children crying and SCDF personnel communicating with some residents in Malay.
Describing the scene as chaotic, another resident, 36, recounted how the personnel knocked on doors to urge people to evacuate quickly. She said they helped young children and a visually impaired elderly person make their way out of the building.
The evacuated residents gathered downstairs, where they remained for some time before being allowed to return to their homes.

标题: Continuing Impact Fifty Years After Latin America’s Deadliest High-Rise Fire - LatinAmerican Post
正文:
This year, Brazil marked the fiftieth anniversary of the Joelma Building fire in São Paulo, which claimed the lives of nearly 200 people, becoming Latin America’s deadliest high-rise disaster. The harrowing stories of the victims and the lessons learned from this tragedy continue to shape fire safety regulations today.
On the morning of February 1, 1974, the bustling city of São Paulo, Brazil, was shaken by one of the most catastrophic fires in its history. At approximately 8:50 a.m., a fire broke out in the 25-story Joelma Building, home to Banco Crefisul’s offices. The fire, which spread rapidly due to a malfunctioning air conditioner on the 12th floor, consumed much of the building within just 20 minutes, leaving those inside with little time to escape.
Like many skyscrapers, the Joelma Building lacked basic fire safety measures, such as fire alarms, sprinkler systems, and fireproof exits. Without proper firewalls, emergency lighting, or evacuation plans, the building quickly became a death trap for its occupants. The single, non-fireproof stairwell that served as the only emergency egress soon filled with thick smoke and intense heat, making it impassable after the 11th floor.
When firefighters arrived 20 minutes after the fire began, the building was engulfed in flames. Their equipment was inadequate to handle such a large blaze, with ladders reaching only the 14th floor—leaving hundreds of people above the flames stranded. The fire’s ferocity and the building’s lack of preparedness turned the Joelma fire into one of the deadliest high-rise disasters in history.
As the fire spread, nearly 300 people were able to escape the building using the elevators before the shafts filled with smoke, rendering them unusable. 标题: In Poland, Three Men Use a Stretched Blanket to Save a Four-Year-Old Girl Who Fell from the Fifth Floor - Around Prague
正文:
In a Polish town, three passers-by saved the life of a four-year-old girl who fell from a fifth-floor balcony. The men managed to stretch out a blanket in time to cushion the child's fall after she had climbed onto the balcony of a neighbouring, empty apartment and tumbled off.
According to Grzegorz, the owner of a local shop who witnessed the incident, it all began around two o'clock in the afternoon. "I stepped out of the shop into the storeroom and heard people shouting. I ran around the corner, looked up and saw a child on the railing," he told the newspaper Fakt. He immediately ran under the balcony, ready to catch the girl with his bare hands if she fell. Soon two other passers-by joined him, one of whom happened to be carrying a blanket.
"I was shouting at her to climb back, but she wasn't reacting at all. She even managed to climb over to the other side of the balcony. We moved with the blanket to follow her — and that's when she fell," the rescuer continued. The girl bounced off the blanket and hit the ground, but the cushioned fall spared her from serious injury. "She only had a dislocated arm and not a single scratch otherwise. She probably just got a bit bruised," the man noted. Firefighters and paramedics soon arrived at the scene and took the child to hospital.
The girl's mother appeared only several minutes later — she had been asleep at the moment of the fall. It later emerged that her blood alcohol level was 0.7 per mille. "I couldn't wake her up, I kept banging on the door for a long time. When she finally opened it, she was groggy and came downstairs slowly, while I kept urging her, telling her the child needed help right away," one neighbour recalled. "She was completely out of it," the woman added.
It is still unclear how long the four-year-old had been alone on the balcony. She had managed to climb over the partition separating two balconies and end up on the balcony of the neighbouring, vacant apartment — and it was from there that she fell.

标题: 高层住宅火情危急，15岁女孩一通电话救了一家人 - 新湖南
正文:
高层住宅火灾一旦发生，浓烟往往会迅速封堵楼梯间，想要下楼逃生的路可能转瞬消失。面对这种情形，是固守待援还是出门逃生？日前，广东东莞一名15岁女孩用一次冷静报警和科学判断，给出了答案。
10月7日，广东省东莞市一高层居民住宅突发火灾，楼内有多名人员被困。接警后，消防救援力量迅速赶赴现场展开营救。经初步调查认定，起火点位于4楼住户卧室床头，系正在充电的充电宝发生热失控，高温引燃床垫，导致火势快速蔓延。经全力救援，被困人员全部安全撤离，事故未造成人员伤亡。
面对顺着楼道向上倒灌的浓烟，身处15楼的一家人同样陷入困境。危急时刻，家中一名15岁女孩迅速拨通119报警电话，清晰、准确地向接警员说出所在楼层和被困情况。在接警员的远程安抚与专业指导下，一家人没有盲目冲入浓烟逃生，而是立刻转移至远离火源的房间，紧闭房门，利用湿毛巾、衣物封堵门缝，原地固守等待救援。最终，全家平安获救。
消防部门表示，很多人潜意识里面对火灾第一时间就是迅速撤离，但在高层火场中，浓烟向上蔓延速度极快，盲目开门逃生极易吸入有毒烟气，几分钟内就能丧失行动能力。因此，在火灾初期快速科学研判现场形势非常重要。
大声呼救，立即通知所有家人。如果火势尚小，如垃圾桶、被褥起火，立即使用灭火器或大量水进行扑救。如果火势已无法控制，立即放弃扑救，呼喊家人一起撤离，离开时关闭户门以延缓火势蔓延。逃出后，到安全地带立即拨打119求助。
先判烟情。严禁盲目开门冲楼，先触摸门板、门把手感受温度，轻开门缝观察楼道烟情；拨打119报警，准确告知所处具体位置、被困人数和火势情况。
无烟速撤。楼道、楼梯间无烟、视线清晰时，立刻弯腰低姿前行，用湿毛巾捂住口鼻或戴上防烟面罩，沿疏散楼梯迅速逃生，撤离途中随手关闭防火门。
有烟固守。楼道出现烟气时，不要贸然向外突围，迅速退回室内紧闭房门，固守待援；用湿毛巾、湿床单等封堵门缝，阻隔烟气渗入；在窗口用手机闪光灯、手电筒、挥舞鲜艳衣物等方式呼救。
走防烟楼梯间。迅速通过最近的防烟楼梯间向下逃生，撤离途中随手关闭楼层防火门，阻隔烟火向下蔓延；切记不可乘坐电梯，避免电梯断电停运、浓烟涌入被困。
高层火场，逃生选择一念之间。能逃则有序撤离，无法逃生就科学固守，掌握正确自救方法，关键时刻就能为自己和家人争取一线生机。

正文:
One person was killed in a two-alarm apartment fire in Washington Heights Saturday, the FDNY said.
The victim was said to be an elderly man who was a hoarder, according to building residents.
Flames broke out on the fourth-floor of the five-story building at 815 West 180th St., near Pinehurst Avenue, at around 6:10 a.m., authorities said.
More than 100 firefighters responded to the scene to fight the morning blaze in the bitter cold, with temperatures in single digits.
The two-alarm blaze was deemed under control around 9:15 a.m.

标题: Woman, 86, dies in Queens NYCHA apartment fire; week’s fourth deadly NYC blaze - New York Daily News
正文:
An 86-year-old woman died as a fire tore through her Queens apartment early Saturday — the fourth fire death to rock the city in a week, officials said.
The fire erupted in the sixth-floor apartment on 12th St. near 41st Ave. at NYCHA’s Queensbridge South Houses just after 2:15 a.m., the FDNY said.
Neighbors woke up to choking smoke and firefighters banging on their doors, shouting at them to evacuate.
“I don’t know how the smoke got in. Maybe the windows,” said Tyrelle Washington, 24, who lived next door to the senior’s apartment. “I couldn’t breathe. I was like, ‘What’s going on?'”
As he exited his apartment, Washington saw the octogenarian, a Dominican woman and longtime tenant who only spoke Spanish, being taken out on a stretcher with extensive burns to her arms and legs.
“She wasn’t moving. Her skin was burned,” Washington said. “I was on edge. I’ve known her since I grew up here. She’s been here quite a while.”
EMS rushed the woman to Mount Sinai Queens, where she died a short time later. Her name was not immediately disclosed.
Once everyone was allowed back into their apartments, Washington peered into the senior’s home. The door had been left ajar.
“It was just black in there,” he said. “You could tell something happened in her apartment. I just can’t fathom this. It just doesn’t make sense to me.”
Residents remembered the senior as a sociable, active woman, who would play cards and bingo with other seniors in a nearby park.
“She didn’t smoke, she didn’t drink. She used to play bingo with the old ladies in the park in the summer,” remembered one 72-year-old tenant, who only wanted to be identified as Cesar, who appeared moved by her death.
“Why wouldn’t I be sad?” he said solemnly. “She was a nice lady.”
The FDNY put out the flames within a half hour. No other injuries were reported.
Saturday’s blaze was the fourth fatal fire to occur since Nov. 9, a day after Firefighter Patrick Brady died of a heart attack while fighting a blaze atop a Brooklyn apartment

Officer Michael Leonhauser responded to the fire at the Levittown Trace Apartments on the 300 block of Ford Road around 5:30 a.m. Body camera footage shows him running door to door inside the smoke-filled building, alerting residents to the danger.

标题: 江西一楼房起火，45人待在家中均获救，选择逃生为何3死1伤？ - 凤凰网
正文:
去年4月江西某小区住宅楼一楼门厅因电动自行车起火引发火灾浓烟瞬间吞噬了唯一的逃生通道——楼梯间
在这场火灾中，一个令人痛心的对比发人深省：从5楼和8楼向下逃生的4人中，3人不幸遇难，1人受伤；而选择紧闭家门、等待救援的45人，则全部安全获救。
很多人认为，只要火在自家楼上，就可以毫不犹豫地向下逃生，这其实是一个误区。此时，如果楼梯间无浓烟、门可正常关闭，可以立即向下跑，不要停留。但如果楼道有浓烟充斥，就不能往下跑。
南昌市消防救援支队高新消防大队宣教员王嘉豪：“如果说我们这个着火点是在你的楼下，那么这个时候着火点是在你的逃生路径上的，我们这个时候就最好还是把房门紧闭，回到家中等待消防的救援。”
在这种情况下，要做好防烟保护，可以用湿毛巾或打湿的床单堵住防盗门缝隙，然后可以通过窗户向外呼救，吸引消防人员的注意。王嘉豪介绍道。
高层建筑起火后，如果着火点在自家楼上，是否就相对安全了？南昌市消防救援支队高新消防大队宣教员王嘉豪表示，这也要见机行事，不能掉以轻心直接往下冲。
王嘉豪提醒：“这时需要先打开房门观察。如果外层楼道没有浓烟，可以迅速撤离；但如果遇到电梯井或楼层内部管线燃烧，形成立体式燃烧，浓烟会短时间内充斥整个楼道。”这个时候就不能轻易地离开自己的房间，室内反而更加安全。要根据现场的情况判断是否往外跑。
专业人士介绍，遇到高层建筑着火，“跑”与“不跑”、“向上”与“向下”的决策关键点不能靠猜，而是要依靠现场情况冷静判断。
首先看起火点是否在逃生路径上。楼下起火，向下跑的路径被阻后，在家等待救援就更安全。
再次就是观察楼道内是否有大量有毒气体浓烟。楼道内有浓烟的情况下，躲在家中更加安全。
“一个是我们这个浓烟往上蔓延，所以上层的空气环境一定是更加差的。第二个就是我们现在的居民楼当中，楼顶上一般是封闭的，往上跑反而会减少你的逃生机会。”王嘉豪解释道。

An apartment building fire in Jersey City, New Jersey, displaced about 30 people Friday, sending them out into frigid temperatures.
Firefighters had to deal with treacherous conditions as they rescued several residents trapped inside.
Fire tore through the lower levels of the building on Winfield Avenue just after 11 a.m.
"We had fire on two different floors. The fire started on the floor of the first floor and went up all the walls to the second and third floor," Jersey City Fire Chief Jack Johnson said.

"The fire department was so nice, and they banged on the door. They wouldn't stop knocking," she said.
The chief says a fire captain is recovering after suffering a laceration to his face, but that there were no other injuries.
The American Red Cross is now helping the displaced residents of the 16-unit building.
Residents were allowed back inside to get some essential belongings.
